title: Independence of the finite coefficient field
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $K_0$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism, fix a prime $\ell$ whose image in $K_0$
is invertible, and fix an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$. Let
$K_{\Qlb}\in D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ be an object of the common-stage category of
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represented at the finite
coefficient stages $E\subset L\subset\Qlb$ by $K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ and $K_L\in
D^b_c(X,L)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with fixed representing isomorphisms $\alpha_E:(E,K_E)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{\Qlb}$ and $\alpha_L:(L,K_L)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{\Qlb}$ in the common-stage category. Then the two objects

$$
 Rf_!K_E\otimes_E\Qlb,\qquad Rf_!K_L\otimes_L\Qlb
$$

of $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$, formed from the compact-support functor
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], are canonically
isomorphic relative to the specified representing isomorphisms. The comparison is independent of the common finite overfield and morphism representatives used to compute it.

proof.text: For every inclusion E ≤ L choose the integral comparison b and rational comparison β of [lem-weil-compact-support-normalized-scalar-isomorphisms], retaining its finite tensor-unit mate specification, whole-system normalization and rational component equality. Apply [lem-weil-compact-support-normalized-scalar-descent] to this entire family to obtain its tower equation. Choices are of the prescribed normalized maps, not arbitrary compact-support values.

proof.text: Present the stage systems of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] by their specified transition functors and associators; stageSystem_existsUnique identifies these presentations with the recorded systems. The finite functors and β form a StageSystem.Morphism: its coherence field is precisely the reversed tower equation of step 1. The concrete quotient functor already built into [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action] sends a representative to β at the source followed by the finite functor map followed by inverse β at the target. Thus no normalization to strict identity transitions and no additional abstract descent theorem is required for this existing quotient.

source.place: Finite scalar compatibility, descent of functors, and comparison paragraphs; concrete StageSystem assembly

proof.text: The object equality of [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action] identifies each finite integral functor value with the specified integral compact-support value. Raw localization and pairing at the same field identify the descended value with [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Package the StageSystem.Morphism, these finite/value equalities, b, its mate specification and its rational component equality into SfCompactSupportCoefficientAction.

source.place: Finite scalar compatibility, descent of functors, and comparison paragraphs; concrete StageSystem assembly

proof.text: Unfold representative: it is the image of the represented input arrow under the concrete quotient functor, conjugated by value_eq. Equal represented arrows therefore give equal output representatives by congruence. Unfold comparison: its hom is the same conjugated functor image of α_E.hom followed by α_L.inv. The representative formula follows by substitution. Identity and composition follow from map_id and map_comp, cancellation of the representing isomorphisms, and cancellation of the value_eq transports.
